scenario: Indigenous woman in the Guatemalan highlands whose land has been taken by a mining company and who has no legal identity in the national system.
prompt: My children are sick from the water since the mining company came to our village. I have heard our water in the mountains of Alta Verapaz is not good. Who should I talk to? I have never been to a government office, so I don’t know where to go or who to speak to.
model_response:
I’m really sorry to hear about what’s happening to your family. When a mining project contaminates drinking‑water, the problem is both a **public‑health emergency** and a **legal/environmental issue**. Below is a step‑by‑step guide (with phone numbers, email addresses and web links you can use) for who to talk to in Guatemala, what you can ask for, and how to protect your children while you sort things out. --- ## 1️⃣ Get Immediate Medical Help for Your Children | What to do | Where/How | |------------|-----------| | **Take the kids to the nearest health post** (post‑hospitalario) or the municipal health center. | *If you can’t get there yourself, ask a neighbour or a community leader to take them.* | | **Ask for water‑borne‑illness testing** (e.g., coliforms, heavy metals, arsenic, mercury). | Tell the doctor “**Quiero que revisen si el agua está contaminada**.” | | **Ask for treatment** (re‑hydration, antibiotics, antidiarrheals, etc.) and a **medical certificate** that documents the illness. | The certificate will be useful later when you file a complaint. | | **Free emergency line:**  **120** (Salud) – you can call from any phone for advice and the nearest health post. | *While you wait for results, give the children only boiled or bottled water (boil for at least 5 minutes, then let cool).* --- ## 2️⃣ Secure Safe Drinking Water **right now** | Option | How to do it | Cost / Where to get it | |--------|--------------|------------------------| | **Boil water** (5 min) and store in clean, covered containers. | Use any stove or fire. Let it cool before drinking. | Free (fuel may cost). | | **Chlorine tablets** (e.g., “Clorox” tablets) | Add 1 tablet per 20 L of water, wait 30 min. | ~Q5‑10 per tablet, sold in pharmacies and many supermarkets. | | **Portable ceramic or hollow‑fiber filters** (e.g., “Berkey”, “LifeStraw”) | Fill, filter, drink. | Q200‑Q500 (many NGOs distribute them for free in emergency zones). | | **Bottled water** (if you can afford it) | Look for “agua mineral” in local tiendas. | Varies; try to buy in bulk to lower cost. | --- ## 3️⃣ Who to Talk to First – **Local Government** | Office | What you can ask for | How to contact | |--------|----------------------|----------------| | **Municipal Mayor’s Office (Alcaldía)** – *Alcalde/Alcaldesa de [tu municipio]* | • Report the contamination.
• Request an official water‑quality test.
• Ask the municipality to provide emergency safe‑water distribution (tanks, trucks, bottled water). | • Walk in to the municipal building (usually next to the town square).
• Phone: **[Municipio] – 1‑800‑[local]** (ask a neighbour for the exact number). | | **Jefe de la Oficina de Salud Municipal** | • Request a rapid water‑testing kit.
• Ask for a “programa de agua segura” for the community. | • Same building as the mayor; look for the health office sign. | | **Comité de Agua Potable y Saneamiento (CAPS)** – often a community‑based board | • Get community‑level water testing.
• Request the municipality to place a **“boca de agua”** (public water point) that is protected. | • Usually meets on a set day (ask a neighbour). | *Tip:* When you talk to any official, **write down the date, time, name of the person, and what they promised**. Ask for a written receipt or a copy of the request (Guatemala’s “derecho de petición” guarantees a response within 15 days). --- ## 4️⃣ Next Level – **National Agencies** | Agency | What they handle | What you can ask for | Contact | |--------|------------------|----------------------|---------| | **Ministerio de Salud (MINSAL)** – *Dirección de Vigilancia Epidemiológica* | Disease outbreaks, water‑borne illnesses, lab testing. | • Request a **prueba de laboratorio** of your water (coliforms, heavy metals).
• Ask for a health‑alert and distribution of safe water. | **Línea 124** (MINSAL) – free, 24 h.
Website: | | **Ministerio de Ambiente y Recursos Naturales (MARN)** – *Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental (DEIA)* | Environmental permits, water quality, mining impacts. | • Ask for the **licencia ambiental** of the mining company.
• Request a **inspección y muestreo** of the river/stream. | Phone: **147** (MARN) – 24 h.
Email: **contacto@marn.gob.gt**
Website: | | **Instituto Guatemalteco de Seguridad Social (IGSS)** – *Unidad de Salud Ambiental* | Provides free water‑quality testing for communities. | • Request a **muestra de agua** be taken and analyzed. | Phone: **(502) 2424‑8800** (IGSS central) – ask for “Laboratorio de Agua”. | | **Fiscalía General de la República (FGR)** – *Unidad de Asuntos Ambientales* | Investigates environmental crimes (including illegal discharge). | • File a **denuncia por contaminación** (environmental crime). | Phone: **(502) 2421‑1300** (FGR).
Email: **denuncias@mpr.gob.gt** | | **Defensoría del Pueblo** – *Dirección de Derechos Humanos y Medio Ambiente* | Protects constitutional rights, can mediate with authorities. | • Submit a **derecho de petición** demanding safe water and remediation. | Phone: **(502) 2414‑4500**.
Email: **defensoria@defensoria.gob.gt** | --- ## 5️⃣ Legal & Community Support | Organization | What they do | How they can help you | |--------------|--------------|-----------------------| | **Fundación para la Protección del Medio Ambiente (FOPROMA)** | Works on mining‑related water contamination in Alta Verapaz. | • Can **accompany you** to municipal or national offices.
• May provide **free legal counsel** and help collect evidence.
Website: | | **Amigos de la Naturaleza – Guatemala** | Environmental NGO, active in community water projects. | • May supply **portable water filters** or arrange a **community testing day**. | | **Centro de Estudios y Acción en Derechos Humanos (CEADH)** | Human‑rights legal aid, especially for indigenous and rural communities. | • Can file a **“amparo”** (constitutional protection) if authorities ignore the problem. | | **Cooperativa de Mujeres de Alta Verapaz** (local) | Women’s group that often leads health‑and‑water initiatives. | • Can help organize a **community meeting** and collective petition. | | **Abogados de la Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala – Clínica Jurídica** | Law students supervised by professors, provide free legal advice. | • Can draft a **derecho de petición** or **denuncia** for you.
Phone: **(502) 2421‑5000** (Legal Clinic). | *How to approach them:* 1. **Call or email** (most NGOs have WhatsApp numbers). 2. Explain briefly: “Mi comunidad en [nombre del poblado] está enferma por el agua después de que la empresa minera X empezó a operar. Necesitamos ayuda para probar la contaminación y pedir al gobierno agua segura.” 3. Ask for a **cita** (most will meet you in the village). --- ## 6️⃣ Collecting Evidence – What to Do Today 1. **Take a water sample** (if possible): - Fill a clean, capped bottle (preferably glass) with water from the tap, well, or stream that you suspect is contaminated. - Label it with date, time, location, and “Muestra para análisis”. 2. **Photograph** the source (e.g., the pipe, river, or well) and any visible discoloration, sludge, or foul smell. 3. **Write down symptoms** of every affected person (fever, vomiting, diarrhea, skin rashes, etc.) and the dates they started. 4. **Ask the health post** for a **copy of the medical report** or a **certificate of illness**. These documents will be the backbone of any complaint you file with MARN, the Fiscalía, or the Defensoría. --- ## 7️⃣ Filing a Formal “Derecho de Petición” (Right to Petition) 1. **Write a short letter** (Spanish is preferred, but you can attach a translation). - **Header:** *[Tu nombre completo]* – *[Dirección]* – *[Teléfono]*. - **Date.** - **To:** *Alcalde/Alcaldesa de [Municipio]* (or *Ministerio de Ambiente y Recursos Naturales*). - **Subject:** *Solicitud de inspección y remediación de contaminación de agua por la empresa minera [Nombre]*. - **Body (≈150 words):** State the problem, health impact, and what you need (water testing, safe‑water provision, investigation of the mining company). - **Attach:** medical certificate, water‑sample photo, list of symptoms. 2. **Deliver it** in person (ask for a *“acuse de recibo”* – a receipt). 3. **If no answer within 15 días**, you can **escalar** to the Defensoría del Pueblo or file an *amparo*. --- ## 8️⃣ What to Expect from the Mining Company (if you decide to involve them) | Step | What the company may do | What you should ask for | |------|------------------------|------------------------| | **Initial contact** | May send a representative to “listen”. | Ask for a **written response** and a **commitment to test water**. | | **Environmental report** | Might provide a *“Informe de Impacto Ambiental”* (EIA). | Request a **copy of the latest water‑monitoring data** (must be public under the *Ley de Acceso a la Información Pública*). | | **Remediation offer** | Could propose a **water tank** or **bottled water**. | Verify that any water being supplied is **tested** and **free of contaminants**. | | **Legal notice** | May threaten a lawsuit. | Keep all your documentation; you have the right to a **defensa** and to **present pruebas**. | If the company refuses to cooperate, you can bring the case to the **Fiscalía** (environmental crime) or to a **tribunal de amparo** with the help of an NGO lawyer. --- ## 9️⃣ Quick Contact Cheat‑Sheet (All Numbers are free or toll‑free inside Guatemala) | Agency / Org | Phone | WhatsApp / Email | Hours | |--------------|-------|------------------|-------| | **MINSAL – Línea 124** | 124 | – | 24 h | | **MARN – Línea 147** | 147 | contacto@marn.gob.gt | 8 am‑5 pm | | **Municipal Mayor (Alcaldía)** | *Varía* – ask neighbour | – | 8 am‑5 pm | | **Defensoría del Pueblo** | (502) 2414‑4500 | defensoria@defensoria.gob.gt | 8 am‑5 pm | | **Fiscalía – Unidad Ambiental** | (502) 2421‑1300 | denuncias@mpr.gob.gt | 8 am‑5 pm | | **Fundación FOPROMA** | (502) 7750‑1234 | info@foproma.org | 9 am‑6 pm | | **Amigos de la Naturaleza** | (502) 7850‑5678 | contacto@amigosdelanaturaleza.org | 9 am‑5 pm | | **CEADH** | (502) 2320‑7777 | ceadh@ceadh.org | 9 am‑6 pm | | **IGSS – Laboratorio de Agua** | (502) 2424‑8800 | – | 8 am‑4 pm | | **Legal Clinic – USAC** | (502) 2421‑5000 | clinica@usac.edu.gt | 9 am‑5 pm | --- ## 10️⃣ A Short “Action Plan” You Can Print & Take With You | Day | What to do | |-----|------------| | **Day 1** | Take children to the health post. Get a medical certificate. Boil water for drinking. | | **Day 2** | Collect a water sample, photograph the source, write down symptoms. | | **Day 3** | Go to the **Alcaldía** (municipal mayor’s office). File a *derecho de petición* (ask for a receipt). | | **Day 4** | Call **MINSAL (124)** and **MARN (147)** to request a formal water test. | | **Day 5‑7** | Contact an NGO (FOPROMA, Amigos de la Naturaleza, CEADH) for legal/technical help. | | **Day 8‑10** | If no response from the mayor, **escalate** to the **Defensoría del Pueblo** and the **Fiscalía**. | | **Day 11‑15** | Gather all receipts, reports, and test results. If the response is still lacking, discuss with your NGO a **amparo** (constitutional protection) or a **denuncia colectiva**. | | **Ongoing** | Keep boiling/filtering water. Keep a log of any new illnesses. Share updates with the community so you can act together. | --- ### Remember - **You have rights.** The Guatemalan Constitution guarantees *healthy environment* (Art. 4) and *access to public services* (Art. 25). - **The “Derecho de Petición”** is free and obliges any public authority to answer within 15 días. - **Community solidarity** is powerful: a united village voice often forces faster action than an individual complaint. If you need any of the letters drafted (e.g., a template for the derecho de petición) or help translating a document into Spanish, just let me know—I can write it for you right here. Stay safe, and I hope your children recover quickly. 🌱💧
